guard: every path that gives up a seat's slot says WHICH path it was and WHAT the runtime saw, and a runtime that cannot see the exit says so instead of reporting a clean one
why: NO BUILD IN `command`, AND THE RUN CHECKS THAT RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT. The suite imports the
subject relatively (`../src/manager.js`), so tsx loads `manager.ts` and `runtime/pty.ts` from
source. `@cotal-ai/core` is reached as a bare specifier and therefore resolves to `dist` — but
this change adds only an OPTIONAL INTERFACE MEMBER to core, which erases at runtime, so nothing
in core's dist participates in any assertion here and no mutation below targets it. If that
reasoning were wrong, mutation 1 would come back SURVIVED.
MUTATION 1 IS THE DEFECT VERBATIM: the log line deleted, which is the shipped state. Every cell
that reads the line must fall.
MUTATIONS 2 AND 3 ARE THE TWO HALVES OF THE LINE, AND THEY ARE NOT REDUNDANT. The incident
needed both facts and they answer different questions: WHICH PATH gave up the slot (a despawn
is not a crash) and WHAT THE RUNTIME SAW (a clean `/exit` is not a SIGKILL). A line carrying
one and not the other still leaves a supervisor unable to explain a death, so each half is
pinned on its own and a change that guts one while leaving the other cannot pass.
MUTATION 4 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST AND IT IS THE TIDY-LOOKING EDIT. Defaulting an absent
`exitInfo` to `code 0` reads like a harmless convenience and is the exact failure this suite
exists to prevent: tmux/cmux/orca/herdr attach to an externally-owned process and genuinely
cannot see how the child ended, so the default would print a FABRICATED CLEAN EXIT on precisely
the seats whose death nobody can account for. Note it is graded against a second cell (a
genuine `code: 0`) so `unavailable` and `clean` can never be collapsed into one another in
either direction.
MUTATION 5 GIVES `FreeSlotCause` A DEFAULT. The compiler currently forces every free path to
name itself; with a default the six callers still work and a SEVENTH path added later would
silently log the wrong cause. It kills on the despawn cell, which is the one whose caller passes
a value the default would override.
MUTATION 6 RESTORES THE DISCARDED PAYLOAD IN THE PTY RUNTIME — the actual root of the missing
information. `proc.onExit(() => …)` threw away the `{ exitCode, signal }` node-pty already
hands it; the manager could not have reported what nothing captured.
MUTATION 7 IS THE CONTROL FOR THE CAPTURE INSTRUMENT. Every graded cell asserts on captured
stderr, so a capture that silently caught nothing would read as `no wrong line was printed`
rather than as a dead instrument, and all nine of those cells would be vacuous together.
NOT GRADED, and said rather than implied: whether the cause each caller passes is the TRUE
cause of that death. These cells prove the plumbing carries and prints whatever the call site
declares; a caller that mislabels its own path would pass every cell here. Six call sites are
labelled by reading them, and nothing automated defends that mapping.
ALSO NOT GRADED, narrowed after the harness refused the first attempt: cells 7-9 spawn real children
and prove the pty runtime captures a real exit code and a real kill signal. They do NOT prove the manager's
line and that capture are wired together end to end through a live spawn — no cell starts a pty child and
then drives freeSlot over it. The two halves are each proven; the seam between them is argued, not measured.
